summary: Jiang and Zhang answer, for generic global Arthur parameters, the Arthur–Schmid question of how to construct a concrete module for a cuspidal automorphic representation from its parameter. For π on an orthogonal or unitary group G_n with generic parameter φ_τ, a cuspidal σ on a smaller group H_m, chosen by the Generic Summand Conjecture 2.3 from the first non-zero Bessel coefficient of π, gives a residual representation E_{τ⊗σ} on H_{a+m}, and its Bessel–Fourier coefficient, the twisted automorphic descent, is shown to be π, or π ⊕ π⋆ for even orthogonal groups, assuming Conjecture 2.3 and the local Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture (Theorem 7.1). The engine is a family of global zeta integrals of Bessel type for G × GL, which unfold to Euler products of local Bessel functionals (Theorems 4.5, 4.7, 4.8), and the reciprocal non-vanishing of Bessel periods (Theorem 5.3). As consequences, one direction of the global Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture holds for these groups (Theorem 5.7), and the other holds under Conjecture 6.8 (Theorem 6.10), unconditionally for SO_{2n+1} × SO_2 (Corollary 6.11). The atlas plans Arthur's, Mok's and KMSW's classification (ML.4), Eisenstein series and intertwining operators (AS.1–AS.2), the L-functions (AL.3–AL.4) and the local Langlands correspondence of GL_n (ET.6). It has nothing on the Gan–Gross–Prasad conjectures, Bessel models or periods, Fourier coefficients along nilpotent orbits, or automorphic descent, and the libraries have none of this. The extraction proposes two new roadmaps: one for the Gan–Gross–Prasad framework, which several queued papers also need, and one for the paper's theory. It routes six items as sources to AS.2, ML.4, ML.5, ET.6 and AF.1, and records five source issues: two misprints and three gaps (the unramified computation rests on an unpublished preprint; the classification for inner forms of orthogonal groups was only outlined; Proposition 2.2 has no proof).

items.name: Classical groups, pure inner forms and relevant pairs
items.statement: Let F be a local or number field of characteristic 0, E = F or a quadratic extension F(√ς), and (V, q) a non-degenerate 𝔫-dimensional space over E, Hermitian if E ≠ F and quadratic if E = F; G_n = Isom(V, q)°, n = [𝔫/2], is a pure inner form of a quasi-split G*_n of the same type (inner twisting by H¹(F, G_n)). For an 𝔪-dimensional non-degenerate subspace (W, q) whose orthogonal complement W⊥ is F-split of odd dimension, H_m = Isom(W, q)° (m = [𝔪/2]) and (G_n, H_m) is a relevant pair; another pair (G′_n, H′_m) of pure inner forms is relevant to it when (W′)⊥ ≃ W⊥ as Hermitian spaces. Over a number field G_n is a pure inner form of G*_n at every place.
items.note: The libraries have groups of points of orthogonal groups of a quadratic map and the unitary group of the standard Hermitian form, not Isom(V, q)° as an algebraic group over F, pure inner forms or relevance.

items.name: Local and global Vogan packets
items.statement: For a relevant pair of quasi-split groups G*_n × H*_m and a local L-parameter φ in Φ̃⁺_unit(G*_n × H*_m) (the localizations of generic global Arthur parameters), the local Vogan packet Π̃_φ[G*_n × H*_m] (3.4) is the union of the local L-packets Π̃_φ(G_n × H_m) over all relevant pure inner forms G_n × H_m, with Π̃_φ(G_n × H_m) = ∅ when φ is not G_n × H_m-relevant. The global Vogan packet Π̃_{φ×φ′}[G*_n × H*_m] of a pair of generic global Arthur parameters is formed from the local ones.

items.name: Local Bessel models
items.statement: For a relevant pair (G_n, H_m) over a local field F with 2ℓ + 1 = dim W⊥ = 𝔫 − 𝔪, let p_ℓ = [(2ℓ+1)1^{𝔫−2ℓ−1}], V_{p_ℓ} the associated unipotent subgroup and ψ_{O_ℓ} the generic character of an F-rational orbit O_ℓ such that H_m = H^{O_ℓ}_{ℓ⁻} normalizes V_{p_ℓ} and stabilizes ψ_{O_ℓ}; R_{O_ℓ} := H_m ⋉ V_{p_ℓ}. For π, σ irreducible admissible representations of G_n(F), H_m(F), the local Bessel functionals are Hom_{R_{O_ℓ}(F)}(π ⊗ σ, ψ_{O_ℓ}) (3.5); equivalently Hom_{H_m(F)}(J_{ψ_{O_ℓ}}(π) ⊗ σ, C) with J_{ψ_{O_ℓ}} the twisted Jacquet module.
items.note: The partition is printed with exponent 𝔫 − 2ℓ + 1 on p. 26 (source issue E1); (2.9) has 𝔫 − 2ℓ − 1.

items.name: Uniqueness of local Bessel models
items.statement: For every local field F of characteristic 0 and π, σ as above, dim Hom_{R_{O_ℓ}(F)}(π ⊗ σ, ψ_{O_ℓ}) ≤ 1.
items.locator: Section 3.2, p. 27; used in (2.10), (4.12), (5.14), Section 6.1 (arXiv v4) ([AGRS10], [SZ12], [GGP12], [JSZ10])
items.note: Aizenbud–Gourevitch–Rallis–Schiffmann (p-adic), Sun–Zhu (archimedean), Gan–Gross–Prasad (reduction of the Bessel case), Jiang–Sun–Zhu (archimedean Bessel). Cited; not read.

items.name: The local Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture (Conjecture 3.1)
items.statement: Conjecture: let G*_n and H*_m be a relevant pair of F-quasisplit classical groups over a local field F. For every local L-parameter φ in Φ̃⁺_unit(G*_n × H*_m), Σ_{π ⊗ σ ∈ Π̃_φ[G*_n × H*_m]} dim Hom_{R_{O_ℓ}(F)}(π ⊗ σ, ψ_{O_ℓ}) = 1 (3.6).
items.note: A conjecture used as a hypothesis (Theorem 7.1, Corollaries 7.2, 7.4).

items.name: Known cases of the local conjecture (Theorem 3.2)
items.statement: Conjecture 3.1 holds for: (1) orthogonal pairs over p-adic F, for generic local L-parameters [MW12]; (2) orthogonal pairs over archimedean F, for tempered parameters [Luo, thesis 2020]; (3) unitary pairs over p-adic F or over R, for tempered parameters [Beuzart-Plessis]; (4) unitary pairs over p-adic F, for generic parameters [GI16]. Over R, H. He proves it for discrete series of unitary groups [He17].
items.note: Cited results (Waldspurger, Mœglin–Waldspurger, Beuzart-Plessis, Gan–Ichino, Luo, He); not read. The archimedean generic non-tempered cases remain open, as the paper says.

items.name: Bessel periods
items.statement: For an automorphic form φ_1 on the bigger group and φ_2 on the stabilizer G^{w_0} of the Bessel character, the Bessel period is P^{ψ_{ℓ,w_0}}(φ_1, φ_2) = ∫_{G^{w_0}(F)\G^{w_0}(A)} F^{ψ_{ℓ,w_0}}(φ_1)(g) φ_2(g) dg (4.7), absolutely convergent if one of the forms is cuspidal (Bessel coefficients of forms of moderate growth have moderate growth, and those of rapidly decreasing forms are rapidly decreasing on Siegel sets); for cuspidal π, σ it is written ⟨F^{ψ_{O_ℓ}}(φ_π), φ_σ⟩_{H} (5.6), an L²-inner product (4.8).

items.name: The global Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture (Bessel periods)
items.statement: Conjecture [GGP12, Conj. 24.1, 26.1]: let φ, φ′ be generic global Arthur parameters of a relevant pair G*_n × H*_m. There is a pair (π, σ) in the global Vogan packet Π̃_{φ×φ′}[G*_n × H*_m], with cuspidal realizations, having a non-zero Bessel period ⟨F^{ψ_{O_ℓ}}(φ_π), φ_σ⟩ if and only if L(1/2, φ × φ′) ≠ 0; such a pair is then unique (given the local conjecture at every place).
items.locator: Section 1, p. 4; Sections 5.5 and 6.3, pp. 55–57, 69–70 (arXiv v4)
items.note: The paper proves one direction in general (Theorem 5.7) and the other under Conjecture 6.8 (Theorem 6.10), without the cuspidal multiplicity one hypothesis of [GGP12]. For simple generic parameters, [GJR04/05/09] has, the paper reports, a gap in the proof of its Proposition 5.3.

items.name: Global Arthur parameters of classical groups
items.statement: Ψ̃_ell(N) is the set of conjugate self-dual elliptic global parameters ψ^N = ⊞_i (τ_i, b_i) of G_{E/F}(N), N = Σ a_i b_i, τ_i ∈ A_cusp(G_{E/F}(a_i)) conjugate self-dual, (τ_i, b_i) pairwise distinct; generic if all b_i = 1 (Φ̃_ell(N)), simple if r = 1. With n^∨ = 𝔫 for unitary and even orthogonal groups and 𝔫 − 1 for odd orthogonal ones, Ψ̃_2(G*_n, ξ) (N = n^∨) consists of the ψ of the form (2.5) attached to a twisted elliptic endoscopic datum (G, s, ξ); τ is of symplectic (resp. orthogonal) type if L^S(s, τ, ∧²) (resp. L^S(s, τ, Sym²)) has a pole at s = 1, and conjugate orthogonal/symplectic according to the pole of the Asai L-function, η_{(τ,b)} = κ_a(−1)^{a+b}. The sign κ of ξ is fixed to be 1.
items.note: ML.4 gives the Arthur/Mok/KMSW classification inputs explicit proof-source owners.

items.name: Theorem 2.1 (endoscopic classification)
items.statement: For every π ∈ A_disc(G_n) there is a G_n-relevant global Arthur parameter ψ ∈ Ψ̃_2(G*_n, ξ) such that π lies in the global Arthur packet Π̃_ψ(G_n). The discrete multiplicity is expected to be 1 unless G_n is even special orthogonal, where it can be 2; for generic packets the local multiplicity property holds at all places, so the multiplicities in generic global packets are known.
items.note: For non-quasi-split orthogonal G_n, Arthur's book gives only an outline (Chapter 9), as the introduction says; source issue E4.

items.name: The outer automorphism Õ(G_n) and the pairs {π, π⋆}
items.statement: Õ(G_n) := Õut_N(G_n) = Aut_N(G_n)/Int_N(G_n) [Art13, Ch. 8]; for G_n even special orthogonal it acts by ε-conjugation, ε ∈ O_{2n}(F) with det ε = −1 and ε² = 1, so the Õ(G_n)-orbit of π is {π} or a torsor {π, π⋆}, and an elliptic ψ^N may descend to two parameters {ψ, ψ⋆} with different packets but the same tensor product L-functions; otherwise Õ(G_n) is trivial. C_π denotes a fixed realization of π in the discrete spectrum.

items.name: Localizations of generic parameters and generic local packets
items.statement: At a place ν the localization φ_ν of a generic global Arthur parameter is a local L-parameter L_{F_ν} → ^L G*_n (L_{F_ν} = W_{F_ν} × SL_2(C) for ν finite, W_{F_ν} for ν archimedean) given by a datum (L*_ν, φ^{L*}_ν, β): a Levi GL_{n_1} × ⋯ × GL_{n_t} × G*_{n_0}, tempered parameters φ_j of GL_{n_j} and φ_0 of G*_{n_0}, and β_1 > ⋯ > β_t > 0, with φ_ν = ⊕_j (φ_j|·|^{β_j} ⊕ φ_j^∨|·|^{−β_j}) ⊕ φ_0; the local L-packet Π̃_{φ_ν}(G*_n) contains a generic member, and all its members are irreducible and unitary (Φ̃⁺_unit).
items.note: Without the Ramanujan conjecture the localizations need not be tempered, hence the exponents β.

items.name: The local Langlands correspondence for GL_n
items.statement: The local Langlands correspondence for GL_n over local fields of characteristic 0 ([Lan89], [HT01], [Hen00], [Sch13]).
items.locator: Section 3.1, p. 24; Section 4.6, p. 45; Appendix B, p. 85 (arXiv v4)
items.note: ET.6 plans the p-adic correspondence with full Weil–Deligne parameters. The archimedean case (Langlands) is routed to AF.1 by PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20.

items.name: Tensor product L-functions through Arthur parameters
items.statement: For π, σ cuspidal with generic global Arthur parameters, L(s, τ × π) := L(s, τ × φ_π) and L(s, τ × σ) are defined through the parameters (Rankin–Selberg L-functions of general linear groups), as are the local factors at ramified places; L(s, τ, ρ) for ρ = ∧², Sym² or the Asai representation As ⊗ ξ^m. They are meromorphic in s.
items.note: AL.3 plans GL_n × GL_m Rankin–Selberg L-functions, AL.4 unramified L-group factors, ML.4 the transfer that defines them for classical groups.

items.name: Structure of the classical groups G_n
items.statement: With (V_0, q) the F-anisotropic kernel of (V, q) of dimension 𝔡_0 = 𝔫 − 2𝔯 (𝔯 the Witt index = F-rank of G_n), V = V⁺ ⊕ V_0 ⊕ V⁻ with bases e_1, …, e_𝔯, e′_1, …, e′_{𝔡_0}, e_{−𝔯}, …, e_{−1} (2.1), q(e_i, e_{−j}) = δ_{ij}, q(e′_i, e′_i) = d_i; the matrices J (2.2); the minimal parabolic P_0 = (Res_{E/F}S × G_{𝔡_0}) ⋉ N_0; the relative root system of type B_𝔯, D_𝔯 (orthogonal) or BC_𝔯, C_𝔯 (unitary); standard parabolics P_J = M_J U_J and the maximal P_î with M_î ≅ G_{E/F}(i) × G_{n−i}, G_{E/F}(i) = Res_{E/F}GL_i.

items.name: Fourier coefficients attached to partitions
items.statement: For a quasi-split G*_n, P(𝔫, G*_n) is the set of partitions of type (𝔫, G*_n), parametrizing the F-stable nilpotent orbits O^{st}_p of g*_n(F). An F-rational orbit O_p gives a unipotent V_p and a character ψ_{O_p} of V_p(A) trivial on V_p(F), and F^{ψ_{O_p}}(φ)(g) = ∫_{V_p(F)\V_p(A)} φ(vg) ψ_{O_p}^{−1}(v) dv (2.7), left H^{O_p}(F)-invariant with H^{O_p} = Cent_{N_{G*_n}(V_p)_{ss}}(ψ_{O_p})° (2.8). For π ∈ A_disc with realization C_π, F^{O_p}(C_π) is the ψ_{O_p}-Fourier module, p(π) the set of p with F^{O_p}(C_π) ≠ 0 for some O_p, and p^m(π) its maximal elements; for a pure inner form G_n, p is G_n-relevant if V_p is defined over F.
items.note: Tau Ceti has sl₂-triples, not the classification of nilpotent orbits of classical Lie algebras by partitions or these coefficients.

items.name: Bessel coefficients and Bessel modules
items.statement: For p_ℓ = [(2ℓ+1)1^{𝔫−2ℓ−1}] (G_n-relevant iff ℓ ≤ 𝔯) and π ∈ A_disc(G_n), F^{O_ℓ}(π) := F^{O_{p_ℓ}}(π) is the ℓ-th Bessel module, a space of automorphic functions of moderate growth on H^{O_ℓ}_{ℓ⁻}(A) = Isom(W^{O_ℓ}, q)°(A), where (W^{O_ℓ}, q) is non-degenerate of dimension 𝔩⁻ = 𝔫 − 2ℓ − 1 (ℓ⁻ = [𝔩⁻/2]) and G_n × H^{O_ℓ}_{ℓ⁻} is a relevant pure inner form of G*_n × H*_{ℓ⁻}.

items.name: Proposition 2.2 (cuspidality of Bessel modules)
items.statement: For π ∈ A_cusp(G_n) with a cuspidal realization C_π there is ℓ_0 ∈ {0, 1, …, 𝔯} such that (1) F^{O_{ℓ_0}}(C_π) ≠ 0 but F^{O_ℓ}(C_π) = 0 for all ℓ > ℓ_0; and (2) F^{O_{ℓ_0}}(C_π) is cuspidal: its constant terms along all parabolic subgroups of H^{O_{ℓ_0}}_{ℓ_0⁻} vanish. (ℓ_0 = ℓ_0(C_π) is the first occurrence index.)
items.note: No proof beyond 'one may extend the proof of [GRS11, Theorem 7.3] to the current case' (source issue E5). Part (1) is immediate since ℓ = 0 gives φ itself.

items.name: Multiplicity-free decomposition of the first Bessel module
items.statement: For π ∈ A_cusp(G_n), F^{O_{ℓ_0}}(C_π) embeds in L²_cusp(H^{O_{ℓ_0}}_{ℓ_0⁻}) and decomposes as a multiplicity-free Hilbert direct sum σ_1 ⊕ σ_2 ⊕ ⋯ of irreducible cuspidal representations (2.10).
items.note: Multiplicity freeness from the uniqueness of local Bessel models.

items.name: Conjecture 2.3 (Generic Summand)
items.statement: Conjecture: if π ∈ A_cusp(G_n) has a G_n-relevant generic global Arthur parameter φ ∈ Φ̃_2(G*_n), there are a cuspidal realization C_π with first occurrence index ℓ_0 and an F-rational orbit O_{ℓ_0} in O^{st}_{p_{ℓ_0}} such that some σ ∈ A_cusp(H^{O_{ℓ_0}}_{ℓ_0⁻}) with an H^{O_{ℓ_0}}_{ℓ_0⁻}-relevant generic global Arthur parameter φ_σ ∈ Φ̃_2(H*_{ℓ_0⁻}) and a cuspidal realization C_σ has ⟨F^{ψ_{O_{ℓ_0}}}(φ_π), φ_σ⟩ ≠ 0 for some φ_π ∈ C_π, φ_σ ∈ C_σ.
items.note: A hypothesis of Theorem 7.1; verified in the subregular case (Proposition 7.3).

items.name: Explicit Bessel data
items.statement: V_ℓ is the unipotent group (2.11) (upper-left block z ∈ Z_ℓ, the maximal unipotent of G_{E/F}(ℓ)); ψ_E = ψ_F if E = F and ψ_F(½ tr_{E/F}(x/√ς)) otherwise; for an anisotropic w_0 ∈ (E^{𝔫−2ℓ}, q), ψ_{ℓ,w_0}(v) = ψ_E(Σ_{i=1}^{ℓ−1} z_{i,i+1} + q(y_ℓ, w_0)) (2.12), and H^{w_0}_{ℓ⁻} = Isom(V_{(ℓ)} ∩ w_0^⊥, q)° (2.13). The anisotropic kernel of W_{𝔩⁻} = V_{(ℓ)} ∩ w_0^⊥ has dimension 𝔡_0 ± 1 and its Witt index is 𝔯 − ℓ or 𝔯 − ℓ − 1 accordingly.

items.name: Lemma 2.4
items.statement: If ℓ < 𝔯 (the Witt index of (V_{(ℓ)}, q) is non-zero), there is g ∈ G_{𝔫−2ℓ}(F) = Isom(V_{(ℓ)}, q)°(F) with g·w_0 = e_𝔯 + (−1)^{𝔫+1}(κ/2)e_{−𝔯} for some κ ∈ F^×; hence w_0 may be taken to be y_κ (2.14).
items.note: Proof omitted in the paper ('straightforward'); a Witt-theorem argument.

items.name: Proposition 2.5 (the stabilizer H^{O_ℓ})
items.statement: For O_ℓ determined by w_0 as in Lemma 2.4, H^{O_ℓ}_{ℓ⁻} = H^{w_0}_{ℓ⁻} is defined by an 𝔩⁻-dimensional non-degenerate subspace (W_{𝔩⁻}, q) with a (𝔡_0 − 1)-dimensional anisotropic kernel if y_{−κ} lies in the G_{E/F}(1) × G_{n−ℓ}-orbit of a non-zero vector of (V_0, q), and with a (𝔡_0 + 1)-dimensional one otherwise.

items.name: Proposition 2.6 (every H_m occurs)
items.statement: For every pure inner form H_m of an F-quasisplit classical group H*_m there are a pure inner form G_n of an F-quasisplit G*_n and a datum (p_ℓ, O_ℓ) with m = ℓ⁻ and H_m ≅ H^{O_ℓ}_{ℓ⁻}; moreover G_n × H_m is a relevant pure inner form of G*_n × H*_m.
items.note: 'Easy' from [GGP12]; no proof given.

items.name: The Eisenstein series E(h, φ_{τ⊗σ}, s)
items.statement: For τ = τ_1 ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ τ_r an irreducible unitary isobaric representation of G_{E/F}(a)(A) (τ_i ∈ A_cusp(G_{E/F}(a_i)) pairwise inequivalent; only genericity is needed for the unfolding) and σ an automorphic representation of H_m(A), P_â = M_â U_â the maximal parabolic of H_{a+m} with M_â = G_{E/F}(a) × H_m, λ_s(m, h) = |det m|^s_{A_E}, φ ∈ A(U_â(A)M_â(F)\H_{a+m}(A))_{τ⊗σ} (4.2) and φ_s = λ_s φ: E(h, φ, s) = Σ_{δ ∈ P_â(F)\H_{a+m}(F)} φ_s(δh) (4.3), absolutely convergent for Re(s) ≫ 0 with meromorphic continuation (Langlands); it realizes I_s(τ, σ) = Ind_{P_â(A)}^{H_{a+m}(A)}(τ|det|^s ⊗ σ) (4.10).

items.name: Bessel–Fourier coefficients of E and the global zeta integral
items.statement: For H_{a+m}-relevant p_ℓ = [(2ℓ+1)1^{m+2a−2ℓ−1}] (ℓ ≤ a + r_m), the Bessel–Fourier coefficient F^{ψ_{ℓ,w_0}}(E(·, φ, s))(h) = ∫_{N_ℓ(F)\N_ℓ(A)} E(nh, φ, s) ψ^{−1}_{ℓ,w_0}(n) dn (4.4) with w_0 = y_κ = e_{a+r_m} + (−1)^{m+1}(κ/2) e_{−(a+r_m)} (4.5) (any anisotropic vector of W_0 when ℓ = a + r_m); R^{w_0}_ℓ = G^{w_0}_{m⁻} ⋉ N_ℓ (4.6), m⁻ = 2a + m − 2ℓ − 1. For π ∈ A_cusp(G^{w_0}_{m⁻}) the global zeta integral is Z(s, φ_{τ⊗σ}, φ_π, ψ_{ℓ,w_0}) := P^{ψ_{ℓ,w_0}}(E(φ_{τ⊗σ}, s), φ_π) = ⟨φ_π, F^{ψ_{ℓ,w_0}}(E(φ_{τ⊗σ}, s))⟩ (4.9); it converges absolutely and is holomorphic where E has no pole.

items.name: The zeta integral as a global Bessel functional
items.statement: Away from the poles of E, Z(s, ·) defines an element ℓ_aut of Hom_{R^{w_0}_ℓ(A)}(I_s(τ, σ), π^∨ ⊗ ψ_{ℓ,w_0}) (4.11), a restricted tensor product of local Hom spaces (4.12), each of dimension at most one by the uniqueness of Bessel models (for Re(s) large); so ℓ_aut = c·Π_ν ℓ_ν (4.13).

items.name: Proposition 4.1 (unfolding the Bessel–Fourier coefficient)
items.statement: For Re(s) large, F^{ψ_{ℓ,w_0}}(E(·, φ_{τ⊗σ}, s))(h) = Σ_{ε_β} Σ_η Σ_δ ∫_{N^η_ℓ(A)\N_ℓ(A)} ∫_{N^η_ℓ(F)\N^η_ℓ(A)} φ_s(ε_β η δ u n h) ψ^{−1}_{ℓ,w_0}(un) du dn, where N^η_ℓ = N_ℓ ∩ η^{−1}P^{ε_{0,β}}_ℓ̂ η, the sums run over ε_β = ε_{0,β} ∈ E^0_{a,ℓ}, over η = diag(ε, γ, ε*) in N^0_{β,ℓ,w_0} (with the orthogonality condition on γw_0 when β > max{a − ℓ, 0}), and over δ ∈ G^η_{m⁻}(F)\G^{w_0}_{m⁻}(F).
items.note: Proved by extending [JZ14, Lemmas 3.1–3.2, Prop. 3.3] (the double cosets P_â\H_{a+m}/P_ℓ̂ indexed by E_{a,ℓ}, [GRS11, §4.2]); details by reference.

items.name: Only the open double coset contributes
items.statement: By the cuspidality of φ_π only the Zariski-open double coset in P_â\H_{a+m}/R^{w_0}_ℓ contributes to Z(s, φ_{τ⊗σ}, φ_π, ψ_{ℓ,w_0}): for a ≤ ℓ it equals the integral (4.16) with β = 0, and for a > ℓ the integral (4.17) with β = a − ℓ, η = diag{I_ℓ, γ_0, I_ℓ}, γ_0 in the open double coset with γ_0 w_0 not orthogonal to W⁻_{ℓ,β}.
items.note: The paper also corrects the integration domain of [JZ14, (3.36)] in (4.26).

items.name: Passage to the Whittaker model of τ
items.statement: Combining the integrations over [Z_{β,η}] and [N^η_ℓ] gives φ_s ↦ φ^{Z_a,κ}_s(h) = ∫_{[Z_a]} φ_s(zh) ψ_{Z_a,κ}(z) dz (4.29) with the non-degenerate character ψ_{Z_a,κ} of (4.30); this is an H_{a+m}(A)-equivariant isomorphism I_s(τ, σ) → I_s(W_τ, σ), W_τ the global Whittaker model of τ.
items.note: Uses Fourier expansion along mirabolic subgroups [JZ14, (3.38)]; the global Whittaker model of GL-cusp forms is part of AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.3's unfolding.

items.name: Proposition 4.2 (the twisted Jacquet map J_s)
items.statement: For Re(s) large, J_s(φ_s)(h) = ∫_{U⁻_{a,η}(A)} φ^{Z_a,κ}_s(n ε_{0,β} η h) ψ_{(m+a+ℓ,a−ℓ)}(n) dn (4.33) converges absolutely, and φ_s ↦ J_s(φ_s) restricted to G^{w_0}_{m⁻}(A) is a G^{w_0}_{m⁻}(A)-equivariant map from I_s(τ, σ) to the smooth induction I^{w_0}_s(ψ_{β−1,y_{−κ}}, σ^{w_q^ℓ}) from N^η_{ℓ,β−1}(A)H^η_m(A); with σ′ := σ^{w_q^ℓ} (4.34) this gives I_s(τ, σ) → I_s(W_τ, σ) → I^{w_0}_s(ψ_{β−1,y_{−κ}}, σ′) (4.35).
items.note: Absolute convergence for general groups is deferred to [JSZ] (source issue E3); w_q acts non-trivially on σ only for even special orthogonal H_m.

items.name: Proposition 4.3 (inner Bessel period)
items.statement: For Re(s) large, Z(s, φ_{τ⊗σ}, φ_π, ψ_{ℓ,w_0}) = ∫_g ∫_{[H^η_m]} F^{ψ^{−1}_{β−1,y_{−κ}}}(φ_π)(xg) J_s(φ_s)(xg) dx dg (4.36), g over R^η_{ℓ,β−1}(A)\G^{w_0}_{m⁻}(A), R^η_{ℓ,β−1} = H^η_m ⋉ N^η_{ℓ,β−1}; the inner integral is the Bessel period P^{ψ^{−1}_{β−1,y_{−κ}}}(g ∗ φ_π, J_s(φ_s)(g)) of the pair (π, σ′) (4.37).

items.name: Corollary 4.4
items.statement: If the Bessel period for (π, σ′) is zero, then the global zeta integral Z(s, φ_{τ⊗σ}, φ_π, ψ_{ℓ,w_0}) is zero for all choices of data (case a > ℓ).

items.name: Theorem 4.5 (Euler product, a > ℓ)
items.statement: Let E(φ_{τ⊗σ}, s) be as in (4.3) and π ∈ A_cusp(G^{w_0}_{m⁻}). The global zeta integral converges absolutely and is holomorphic where E has no pole. If φ_π = ⊗φ_{π_ν} and φ_s = ⊗φ_{s,ν} are factorizable and (π, σ′) has a non-zero Bessel period, then for Re(s) large Z(s, ·) = Π_ν Z_ν(s, ·), with the local zeta integrals Z_ν = ∫_{R^η_{ℓ,β−1}(F_ν)\G^{w_0}_{m⁻}(F_ν)} P_ν^{ψ^{−1}_{β−1,y_{−κ}}}(g_ν ∗ φ_{π_ν}, J_{s,ν}(φ_{s,ν})(g_ν)) dg_ν (4.41).

items.name: Corollary 4.6
items.statement: If a ≤ ℓ and the Bessel period for (σ, π) is zero, then the global zeta integral is zero for all choices of data.

items.name: Theorem 4.7 (Euler product, a ≤ ℓ)
items.statement: With the notation of Theorem 4.5 and a ≤ ℓ, the global zeta integral converges absolutely and is holomorphic where E has no pole; if the data are factorizable and (σ, π) has a non-zero Bessel period, then for Re(s) large Z(s, ·) = Π_ν Z_ν(s, ·) with Z_ν = ∫_{N^η_ℓ(F_ν)\N_ℓ(F_ν)} P_ν^{ψ^{−1}_{m,ℓ−a;y_κ,ν}}(n_ν ∗ f_{W^κ_{τ_ν}⊗σ_ν,s}, φ_{π_ν}) ψ^{−1}_{ℓ,w_0,ν}(n_ν) dn_ν (4.46).
items.note: Not used in the paper; included for completeness.

items.name: The local L-factor L(s, τ_ν, π_ν, σ_ν; ρ)
items.statement: L(s, τ_ν, π_ν, σ_ν; ρ) = L(s + ½, τ_ν × π_ν) / (L(s + 1, τ_ν × σ_ν) L(2s + 1, τ_ν, ρ)) (4.47), with ρ = ∧² if H_{m+a} is even orthogonal, Sym² if odd orthogonal, As ⊗ ξ^m if unitary; at ramified finite places the factors are defined through the localized global Arthur parameters of π and σ. For even orthogonal H_m the factors of σ_ν and σ′_ν agree (O_m(C)-conjugate parameters).

items.name: Theorem 4.8 (unramified computation)
items.statement: If all data are unramified and f_{W^κ_{τ_ν}⊗σ_ν,s}, φ_{σ_ν}, φ_{π_ν} are spherical vectors normalized to take the value 1 at the identity, then Z_ν(s, φ_{τ⊗σ′}, φ_π, ψ_{ℓ,w_0}) = L(s, τ_ν, π_ν, σ_ν; ρ) (4.48).
items.note: The proof in this generality is deferred to Jiang–Soudry–Zhang [44], unpublished (source issue E3).

items.name: The global zeta integral formula (4.49)
items.statement: For S a finite set containing the archimedean and ramified places, Z(s, φ_{τ⊗σ′}, φ_π, ψ_{ℓ,w_0}) = Z_S(s, ·) · L^S(s, τ, π, σ; ρ) with Z_S = Π_{ν ∈ S} Z_ν and L^S the partial product of (4.47).

items.name: The leading constant term of E
items.statement: Among the non-zero constant terms of E(·, φ_{τ⊗σ}, s), the one with the highest-order pole at s = ½ is M(ω_0, τ ⊗ σ, s)(φ)(g) = ∫_{U_â(A)} λ_s φ(ω_0^{−1} n g) dn (5.1), and for factorizable φ it equals M(ω_0, τ ⊗ σ, s)_S(φ_S) · L^S(s, τ × σ)L^S(2s, τ, ρ) / (L^S(1 + s, τ × σ)L^S(1 + 2s, τ, ρ)) · λ_{−s}φ^S_{ω_0(τ⊗σ)} (5.2) (Langlands).
items.note: AS.1 derives constant terms as Weyl sums of intertwining operators, AS.2 their factorization; the unramified evaluation uses AL.4's L-group factors.

items.name: Normalized local intertwining operators
items.statement: For ν ∈ S, N(ω_0, τ ⊗ σ, s)_ν := β_ν(s, τ, σ, ψ_F; ρ) · M(ω_0, τ ⊗ σ, s)_ν (5.3) with β_ν = L_ν(1 + s, τ × σ) L_ν(1 + 2s, τ, ρ) ε_ν(s, τ × σ, ψ_F) ε_ν(2s, τ, ρ, ψ_F) / (L_ν(s, τ × σ) L_ν(2s, τ, ρ)) (5.4) (Shahidi's normalization, local factors through Arthur parameters), so that M(ω_0, τ ⊗ σ, s) = N(ω_0, τ ⊗ σ, s) · L(s, τ × σ)L(2s, τ, ρ) / (L(1 + s, τ × σ)L(1 + 2s, τ, ρ)ε(s, τ × σ)ε(2s, τ, ρ)).
items.note: AS.2 constructs normalized intertwiners once their normalizing factors are supplied; routed there.

items.name: Theorem 5.1 = Theorem B.2 (normalized intertwining operators)
items.statement: Let τ = τ_1 ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ τ_r be as in (4.1) and σ ∈ A_cusp(H_m) with a generic global Arthur parameter. For every place ν, N(ω_0, τ ⊗ σ, s)_ν: Ind(|·|^s τ_ν ⊗ σ_ν) → Ind(|·|^{−s} τ*_ν ⊗ σ_ν) is holomorphic and non-zero for Re(s) ≥ ½ (τ*_ν = ι(τ_ν)^∨). Locally (Theorem B.2): for φ⁺ the local component of an H_m-relevant generic global parameter, τ irreducible admissible unitary generic self-dual of G_{E/F}(a)(F) and σ ∈ Π̃_{φ⁺}(H_m), N(ω_0, τ ⊗ σ, s) is holomorphic and non-zero for Re(s) ≥ ½.
items.locator: Section 5.1, Theorem 5.1, p. 48; Appendix B, Theorem B.2 and proof, pp. 85–87 (arXiv v4)
items.note: Proof: for generic σ [CKPSS04, Thm. 11.1]; otherwise the standard modules are irreducible (Proposition B.1), τ and σ are written through the generic unitary duals of GL (exponents < ½), and the operator factors into rank-one operators handled by [MW89] (Re > −1 for tempered GL data), [Kim05], [Wal03, IV.2.1] and [BW00, Lemma 4.4]. The third type is printed with τ(φ_i) for τ_j (source issue E2).

items.name: Proposition 5.2 (poles of E and its residue)
items.statement: Let σ ∈ A_cusp(H_m) have a generic global Arthur parameter φ_σ and τ = τ_1 ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ τ_r (distinct τ_i) with φ_τ of parity different from φ_σ. Then L(s, τ × σ) is holomorphic at s = ½, E(·, φ_{τ⊗σ}, s) has a pole at s = ½ of order at most r, and the order is r iff L(s, τ_i, ρ) has a pole at s = 1 for every i and L(½, τ × σ) ≠ 0. E_{τ⊗σ} denotes the r-th iterated residue at s = ½.

items.name: Special data for the Bessel periods
items.statement: For π ∈ A_cusp(G_n) with G_n-relevant generic parameter φ = φ_τ (τ on G_{E/F}(N), N = n^∨) and a G_n-relevant p_{ℓ*} = [(2ℓ*+1)1^{𝔫−2ℓ*−1}] such that ⟨F^{ψ_{O_{ℓ*}}}(φ_π), φ_σ⟩ ≠ 0 for some σ ∈ A_cusp(H^{O_{ℓ*}}_{ℓ*⁻}) with generic parameter (5.6): take m = ℓ*⁻, 𝔪 = 𝔫 − 2ℓ* − 1, H_m = H^{O_{ℓ*}}_{ℓ*⁻}, a = N (5.7), H_{a+m} ⊃ G_{E/F}(a) × H_m, and p_{κ*} = [(2κ*+1)1^{2a+𝔪−2κ*−1}] with κ* = a − ℓ* − 1 (5.8); then 𝔪⁻ = 𝔫 and G_n is the stabilizer G^{w_*}_{m⁻} for a suitable anisotropic w_* (5.9).

items.name: Theorem 5.3 (reciprocal non-vanishing of Bessel periods)
items.statement: Let σ ∈ A_cusp(H_m) have a generic global Arthur parameter, τ = τ_1 ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ τ_r on G_{E/F}(a)(A), a = N = n^∨, determining a generic parameter φ_τ of G*_n. Assume E_{τ⊗σ′} ≠ 0 and π ∈ A_cusp(G_n) has parameter φ_τ. Then the Bessel period ⟨φ_π, F^{ψ_{O_{κ*}}}(E_{τ⊗σ′})⟩_{G_n} is non-zero for some data iff ⟨F^{ψ_{O_{ℓ*}}}(φ_π), φ_σ⟩_{H_m} is non-zero for some data.
items.locator: Section 5.2, Theorem 5.3, pp. 50–51; proof Sections 5.3–5.4, pp. 51–55 (arXiv v4)
items.note: ⇒ by Corollary 4.4. ⇐: (5.12) with Propositions 5.4–5.6 shows that the pairing with E(·, s) has a pole of order r at ½, which yields E_{τ⊗σ′} ≠ 0 as a conclusion; Section 5.5 uses this without assuming it.

items.name: Proposition 5.4 (normalized local zeta integrals)
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem 5.3, with Z*_ν := Z_ν / L(s, τ_ν, π_ν, σ_ν; ρ) (5.10) and Z(s, ·) = Z*_S(s, ·) L(s, τ, π, σ; ρ) (5.11): (1) Z*_S(s, φ_{τ⊗σ′}, φ_π, ψ_{O_{κ*}}) is meromorphic in s for every smooth section; (2) it is holomorphic at s = ½ for every smooth section (holomorphic at archimedean places, flat at finite ones).
items.note: L(s, τ, π, σ; ρ) has a pole of order r at ½ (from L(s + ½, τ × π)), and the left side of (5.12) has one of order at most r by Proposition 5.2.

items.name: Factorization of the Bessel period
items.statement: For factorizable φ_π = ⊗φ_{π_ν}, φ_σ = ⊗φ_{σ_ν}: ⟨F^{ψ_{O_{ℓ*}}}(φ_π), φ_σ⟩_{H_m} = c_{π,σ} Π_ν b_ν^{ψ_{O_{ℓ*}}}(φ_{π_ν}, φ_{σ_ν}) (5.14), with b_ν the unique (up to scalar) element of Hom_{H_m(F_ν)}(J_{ψ_{O_{ℓ*}}}(π_ν) ⊗ σ_ν, C), equal to 1 on normalized spherical vectors at unramified places and normalized by (A.8) at ν ∈ S.
items.locator: Section 5.3, (5.14), pp. 53–54; Appendix A, (A.8), p. 79 (arXiv v4)

items.name: Proposition 5.5 = Proposition A.1 (local non-vanishing)
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem 5.3, fix s_0 ∈ C. For φ_{σ_ν}, φ_{π_ν} with b_ν^{ψ_{O_{ℓ*}}}(φ_{π_ν}, φ_{σ_ν}) ≠ 0 for every ν ∈ S there is a section φ_{τ_ν⊗σ′_ν} such that Z_S(s, φ_{τ⊗σ′}, φ_π, ψ_{O_{κ*}}) is a non-zero constant at s = s_0. Locally (Proposition A.1): if b_ν(v_{π_ν}, v_{σ_ν}) ≠ 0 then for every s_0 there is a holomorphic section in I_{s,ν}(W_{τ_ν}, σ′_ν) with Z_ν(s_0, ·) ≠ 0.
items.locator: Section 5.3, Proposition 5.5, p. 54; Appendix A, Proposition A.1 and proof, pp. 77–84 (arXiv v4)
items.note: Sections supported in the open cell P_â U⁻_â (A.5), the Bruhat decomposition, reduction to Soudry's integral [Sou17, (4.7)] and the inductive argument of [Sou93, §§6–7] with Dixmier–Malliavin. For p-adic split orthogonal groups it is [Sou17, Prop. 4.1].

items.name: Proposition 5.6
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem 5.3, if (π, σ) has a non-zero Bessel period, there are factorizable φ_π, φ_σ and φ_{τ⊗σ′} with ⟨F^{ψ_{O_{ℓ*}}}(φ_π), φ_σ⟩ ≠ 0 and Z*_S(½, φ_{τ⊗σ′}, φ_π, ψ_{O_{κ*}}) ≠ 0.

items.name: Theorem 5.7 (global Gan–Gross–Prasad: one direction)
items.statement: Let π ∈ A_cusp(G_n) have a G_n-relevant generic global Arthur parameter in Φ̃_2(G*_n)_{G_n} and a cuspidal realization C_π, and suppose ⟨F^{ψ_{O_{ℓ*}}}(φ_π), φ_σ⟩_{H_m} ≠ 0 for some φ_π ∈ C_π, φ_σ ∈ C_σ, σ ∈ A_cusp(H_m) with an H_m-relevant generic global Arthur parameter and cuspidal realization C_σ. Then L(s, π × σ) = L(s, τ × σ) is holomorphic and non-zero at s = ½.
items.locator: Section 5.5, Theorem 5.7, p. 56; proof pp. 55–56 (arXiv v4)
items.note: No multiplicity-one assumption (the even orthogonal case is included). Depends on Theorem 4.8 (source issue E3) and, for non-quasi-split orthogonal groups, on Theorem 2.1 (source issue E4).

items.name: The non-generic parameter ψ_{τ,σ}
items.statement: For φ_τ = (τ_1, 1) ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ (τ_r, 1) ∈ Φ̃_2(G*_n) and σ ∈ A_cusp(H_m) with generic φ_σ ∈ Φ̃_2(H*_m): ψ_{τ,σ} := (τ_1, 2) ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ (τ_r, 2) ⊞ φ_σ (6.1), an H_{a+m}-relevant element of Ψ̃_2(H*_{a+m}).

items.name: Proposition 6.1
items.statement: The residual representation E_{τ⊗σ} is square integrable and, if non-zero, belongs to the global Arthur packet Π̃_{ψ_{τ,σ}}(H_{a+m}).
items.note: 'One may easily verify' as in [JLZ13]; irreducibility of E_{τ⊗σ} is [Mœ11, Thm. B] (Section 6.3).

items.name: Proposition 6.2 (vanishing of large Bessel modules)
items.statement: Let Σ ∈ A_disc(H_{a+m}) lie in Π̃_{ψ_{τ,σ}}(H_{a+m}) and ℓ_0 := (𝔫 − 𝔪 − 1)/2. For every κ with a − ℓ_0 − 1 < κ ≤ a + r_m, the κ-th Bessel modules F^{O_κ}_{κ⁻}(Σ) vanish for all F-rational orbits O_κ in O^{st}_{p_κ}.
items.note: Proof at one unramified place via [GRS11, Thm. 5.1] (local twisted Jacquet modules of the induced representation (6.2)).

items.name: Proposition 6.3 (cuspidality of the κ_0-th Bessel module)
items.statement: For Σ in Π̃_{ψ_{τ,σ}}(H_{a+m}), κ_0 = a − ℓ_0 − 1 and 𝔫 = κ_0⁻, the Bessel modules F^{O_{κ_0}}_n(Σ) are cuspidal sub-representations of L²_cusp(G^{O_{κ_0}}_n) for all F-rational O_{κ_0}.
items.locator: Section 6.1, Proposition 6.3, pp. 59–61 (arXiv v4) ([GRS11, Thm. 7.3], [Mœ08, §1.3], [Mœ11, Thm. B])
items.note: Tower property of [GRS11, Thm. 7.3] with Proposition 6.2; for residual Σ, reduction to E_{τ⊗σ}, which has the least cuspidal support by Mœglin.

items.name: Proposition 6.4
items.statement: For Σ ∈ A_disc(H_{a+m}) the κ-th Bessel module F^{O_κ}_{κ⁻}(Σ) is Õ(G^{O_κ}_{κ⁻})-stable.

items.name: Lemma 6.5 (unramified descent)
items.statement: At a finite place ν where all data are unramified, if Σ_ν is the unique unramified constituent of Ind(τ_ν|det|^{½} ⊗ σ_ν), then the unramified constituents of F^{O_{κ_0}}_n(Σ_ν) have the same Satake parameter as τ_ν under the local Langlands transfer from G^{O_{κ_0}}_n(F_ν) to G_{E/F}(F_ν).
items.locator: Section 6.1, Lemma 6.5 and proof, pp. 62–65 (arXiv v4) ([GRS11, Thms. 5.1, 5.4, 5.6])

items.name: Theorem 6.6
items.statement: For Σ in Π̃_{ψ_{τ,σ}}(H_{a+m}) with F^{O_{κ_0}}_n(Σ) ≠ 0 for some O_{κ_0} (ℓ_0 = (𝔫 − 𝔪 − 1)/2, κ_0 = a − ℓ_0 − 1, κ_0⁻ = 𝔪⁻ = 𝔫): (1) F^{O_{κ_0}}_n(Σ) is cuspidal, a sub-representation of L²_cusp(G^{O_{κ_0}}_n); (2) it is a multiplicity-free Hilbert sum π_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ π_k ⊕ ⋯ of π_i ∈ A_cusp(G^{O_{κ_0}}_n), each with a generic global Arthur parameter in the Õ(G^{O_{κ_0}}_n)-orbit of φ_τ (G^{O_{κ_0}}_n-relevant, determined by τ), and it is Õ(G^{O_{κ_0}}_n)-stable.

items.name: The σ-twisted automorphic descent
items.statement: D^{O_{κ_0}}_n(τ; σ) := F^{O_{κ_0}}_n(E_{τ⊗σ}) (6.9), the σ-twisted automorphic descent of τ from G_{E/F}(N) to G^{O_{κ_0}}_n (N = a = n^∨); Diagram (6.7) (from π, Conjecture 2.3 gives (H_m, σ), then ψ_{τ,σ} and Σ); without σ (m = 0, G_n quasi-split) it is the automorphic descent D^{O_{κ_0}}_n(τ; ∅) = F^{O_{κ_0}}_n(E_τ) of Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry (Diagram (6.8)).

items.name: Conjecture 6.7 (Main Conjecture)
items.statement: Conjecture: let τ = τ_1 ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ τ_r define a G_n-relevant generic global Arthur parameter φ = φ_τ ∈ Φ̃_2(G*_n). For every π ∈ A_cusp(G_n) in Π̃_φ(G_n) there is a datum (H_m, σ) — H_m a pure inner form of a quasi-split H*_m with (G_n, H_m), (G*_n, H*_m) relevant and G_n × H_m a relevant pure inner form of G*_n × H*_m, and σ ∈ A_cusp(H_m) in Π̃_{φ′}(H_m) for an H_m-relevant generic φ′ ∈ Φ̃_2(H*_m) — such that (a) if G_n = G^{O_{κ_0}}_n is not even special orthogonal, or is even special orthogonal with Õ(G_n)-orbit {π}, then D^{O_{κ_0}}_n(τ; σ) ≅ π; (b) if G_n is even special orthogonal with Õ(G_n)-orbit {π, π⋆}, then D^{O_{κ_0}}_n(τ; σ) ≅ π ⊕ π⋆.
items.note: The special case of the Principle of concrete modules.

items.name: The partitions p_{φ,φ′} and p¹_{φ,φ′}
items.statement: p(E_{τ⊗σ}) is the set of H_{a+m}-relevant partitions with a non-zero Fourier coefficient of E_{τ⊗σ}. p_{φ,φ′} := [(a+m−1)(a+1)] if H*_m = SO_{2m}, [(a+m)(a−1)1] if H*_m = SO_{2m+1}, [(a+m)a] if H*_m is unitary; p¹_{φ,φ′} := [(a+m−1)1^{a+1}] if H*_m = SO_{2m} and [(a+m)1^a] otherwise. The conjecture of [Jia14, §4] asserts p ≤ p_{φ,φ′} for all p ∈ p(E_{τ⊗σ}) and all σ in Π̃_{φ′}[H*_m].

items.name: Conjecture 6.8
items.statement: Conjecture: for the pair of generic parameters (φ, φ′) there is σ ∈ Π̃_{φ′}[H*_m] with a cuspidal realization C_σ on H_m(A) such that p¹_{φ,φ′} ∈ p(E_{τ⊗σ}).

items.name: Proposition 6.9
items.statement: Conjecture 6.8 holds when m = 0, for all F-quasisplit H*_a [GRS11], and when m = 1 for the even special orthogonal groups H_{2n+1} = SO_{2n+2,2n} [JLXZ16].
items.note: Cited results; the notation SO_{2n+2,2n} is the paper's.

items.name: Theorem 6.10 (global Gan–Gross–Prasad: the other direction)
items.statement: Let τ be as in (4.1), a = n^∨ = N, with generic φ = φ_τ ∈ Φ̃_2(G*_n), and φ′ a generic global Arthur parameter of H*_m with L(½, φ × φ′) ≠ 0. Assume Conjecture 6.8 for (φ, (φ′)^{w_q^ℓ}). Then there are a cuspidal π in the global Vogan packet Π̃_φ[G*_n] and a cuspidal σ in Π̃_{φ′}(H_m), with cuspidal realizations C_π, C_σ, such that (π, σ) lies in Π̃_{φ×φ′}[G*_n × H*_m] and ⟨F^{ψ_{O_{ℓ_0}}}(φ_π), φ_σ⟩_{H_m} ≠ 0 for some φ_π ∈ C_π, φ_σ ∈ C_σ, where ℓ_0⁻ = m and O_{ℓ_0} is an F-rational orbit in O^{st}_{p_{ℓ_0}}, p_{ℓ_0} = [(2ℓ_0+1)1^{𝔫−2ℓ_0−1}].
items.locator: Section 6.3, Theorem 6.10 and proof, pp. 71–72 (arXiv v4)
items.note: No multiplicity-one assumption.

items.name: Corollary 6.11 (global Gan–Gross–Prasad for SO_{2n+1} × SO_2)
items.statement: Let G*_n be split SO_{2n+1}, φ = φ_τ ∈ Φ̃_2(G*_n) as in (4.1), and φ′ a generic global Arthur parameter of H*_1, an anisotropic SO_2 over F. Equivalent: (1) there are π ∈ Π̃_{φ_τ}[G*_n] and σ ∈ Π̃_{φ′}[H*_1] with ⟨F^{ψ_{O_{ℓ_0}}}(φ_π), φ_σ⟩_{H_1} ≠ 0 for some φ_π ∈ π, φ_σ ∈ σ; (2) L(½, τ × φ′) ≠ 0.
items.note: From Theorems 5.7 and 6.10 with Proposition 6.9; the cuspidal multiplicities are one here.

items.name: Principle 1.1 (concrete modules)
items.statement: Principle: for G a pure inner form of a quasi-split classical group G* and π ∈ A_cusp(G) with a G-relevant global Arthur parameter ψ ∈ Ψ̃_2(G*), there is a datum F(π, G) (information on the Fourier coefficients of π) from which a concrete irreducible module M(ψ, F(π, G)) with π ≅ M(ψ, F(π, G)) can be constructed; if π has cuspidal multiplicity one, π = M(ψ, F(π, G)).
items.note: A guiding principle answering the Arthur–Schmid question; not a theorem. Conjecture 6.7 is its precise form for generic parameters.

items.name: Theorem 7.1 (cuspidal automorphic modules)
items.statement: Conjectures 2.3 and 3.1 imply Conjecture 6.7: for π ∈ A_cusp(G_n) with G_n-relevant generic parameter φ, the module D^{O_{κ_0}}_n(τ; σ) = F^{O_{κ_0}}_n(E_{τ⊗σ}) built from the (H_m, σ) of Conjecture 2.3 is ≅ π, or π ⊕ π⋆ when the Õ(G_n)-orbit of π is {π, π⋆}.
items.locator: Section 7.1, Theorem 7.1 and proof, pp. 73–75 (arXiv v4)
items.note: Proof: Theorem 5.3 gives F^{ψ_{O_{κ_0}}}(E_{τ⊗σ′}) ≠ 0; Theorem 6.6 decomposes it; Theorem 5.3 again and the local conjecture at every place single out π (or π⋆) as the unique distinguished member of its global Vogan packet.

items.name: Corollary 7.2 (regular orbit)
items.statement: Let G*_n be F-quasisplit and π ∈ A_cusp(G*_n) generic with global Arthur parameter (3.1) and τ as in (4.1). Then Conjecture 6.7 holds for π under Conjecture 3.1.
items.note: Here Conjecture 2.3 holds without (H_m, σ) and the construction is the automorphic descent of Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry; irreducible for split SO_{2n+1} by [JS03].

items.name: Proposition 7.3 (subregular orbit)
items.statement: Let φ = φ_τ be a generic global Arthur parameter of G*_n as in (3.1). If a cuspidal member π of the global Vogan packet Π̃_φ[G*_n] has p^m(π) = {p_subr}, the partition of the subregular nilpotent orbit, then Conjecture 2.3 holds for π.
items.note: Case by case: SO_{2n} (H_m a form of SO_3, via [JLS16, Thm. 11.2]), SO_{2n+1} (a form of SO_2), U_{2n} (U_1), U_{2n+1} (a form of U_2).

items.name: Corollary 7.4 (subregular orbit)
items.statement: If π ∈ A_cusp(G_n) has a G_n-relevant generic global Arthur parameter in Φ̃_2(G*_n) and p^m(π) contains the subregular partition p_subr of type (𝔫, G*_n), then Conjecture 6.7 holds for π under Conjecture 3.1.

items.name: The automorphic descent of Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry
items.statement: For an F-quasisplit G*_n and a generic isobaric τ determining a generic global Arthur parameter of G*_n, the descent F^{O_{κ_0}}_n(E_τ) of the residual representation E_τ (parameter (τ_1, 2) ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ (τ_r, 2)) is a non-zero generic cuspidal representation of G*_n(A) with transfer τ [GRS11]; it is irreducible for split SO_{2n+1} [JS03]; and a generic π ∈ A_cusp(G*_n) has such a τ as its transfer ([CKPSS04] with [GRS11]).
items.note: A known functorial transfer; routed to ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.5, where PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25 routed the image of CKPSS functoriality.

items.name: Local twisted Jacquet modules of unramified induced representations
items.statement: [GRS11, Thms. 5.1, 5.4, 5.6]: explicit computation of the twisted Jacquet modules with respect to (V_{p_κ}, ψ_{O_κ}) of unramified representations induced from (µ_1∘det_2) ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ (µ_{[a/2]}∘det_2) ⊗ δ_1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ δ_{r_m}: vanishing above the critical κ and, at the critical κ, a constituent of an explicit unramified principal series of the stabilizer.
items.locator: Section 6.1, proofs of Proposition 6.2 and Lemma 6.5, pp. 58–65 (arXiv v4)
items.note: Cited; [GRS11] not read.

items.name: The tower property for Fourier coefficients
items.statement: [GRS11, Thm. 7.3]: a criterion, in terms of the vanishing of the terms of [GRS11, (7.35)], for the cuspidality of the Bessel coefficients at the first non-vanishing level of the tower.
items.locator: Section 2.3, p. 19; proof of Proposition 6.3, pp. 59–61 (arXiv v4)
items.note: Cited; [GRS11] not read.

items.name: Mœglin's results on residual representations
items.statement: [Mœ08, Thm. §1.3], [Mœ11, Thm. B]: among the residual representations in Π̃_{ψ_{τ,σ}}(H_{a+m}), E_{τ⊗σ} has the least cuspidal support, and E_{τ⊗σ} is irreducible.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 6.3, p. 60; Section 6.3, p. 70 (arXiv v4)
items.note: Cited; not read.

items.name: Soudry's inductive non-vanishing argument
items.statement: The inductive argument of [Sou93, §§6–7]: an integral of the form ∫ |det g|^{s+ρ_a−ℓ} W^κ_{τ_ν}(diag(g, I_{ℓ+1})) b_ν(π(diag(g, I_{m+1}, g*)) v_π, v_σ) dg over Z_{a−ℓ−1}\GL_{a−ℓ−1}(E_ν) vanishing for all data forces W^κ_{τ_ν}(I_a) b_ν(v_π, v_σ) = 0.
items.note: Cited; [Sou93] not read.

items.name: Proposition B.1 (irreducible standard modules)
items.statement: If φ is a generic L-parameter of H*_m of the form (B.1), then every representation in Π̃_φ(H_m), for every pure inner form H_m, is an irreducible standard module: the induced representations Ind(τ(φ_1)|det|^{β_1} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ τ(φ_t)|det|^{β_t} ⊗ σ_0) (B.2), σ_0 ∈ Π̃_{φ_0}(H_{n_0}), are irreducible.
items.locator: Appendix B, Proposition B.1, p. 85 (arXiv v4) ([MW12], [GI16, Prop. 9.1], [Hei16], [ABV92, Thm. 1.24])
items.note: Cited results; routed to ML.4, which owns the local packets.

items.name: The generic unitary dual of GL_n over p-adic fields
items.statement: [Tad86]: every irreducible generic unitary representation of GL_a over a non-archimedean field is an irreducible representation induced from tempered representations and complementary-series pairs with exponents in (0, ½); in particular a (conjugate) self-dual generic unitary τ of G_{E/F}(a)(F) is isomorphic to Ind(τ_1|det|^{α_1} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ τ_d|det|^{α_d} ⊗ τ_0 ⊗ τ*_d|det|^{−α_d} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ τ*_1|det|^{−α_1}) with τ_i unitary generic tempered and ½ > α_1 > ⋯ > α_d > 0 (B.6); likewise the generic members of Π̃_{φ⁺}(H*_m) have the form (B.2) with exponents ½ > β_1 > ⋯ > β_t > 0 (B.5).
items.note: Routed to ET.6, which develops the segment and Langlands-quotient theory of GL_m.

items.name: The generic unitary dual of GL_n over archimedean fields
items.statement: [Vog86]: the same description of the irreducible generic unitary representations of GL_a over R and C, giving (B.5) and (B.6) at archimedean places.
items.note: Routed to AF.1 (real reductive representation theory).

items.name: The Dixmier–Malliavin lemma
items.statement: Every smooth vector of a smooth Fréchet representation of a real Lie group is a finite sum of vectors π(f)v with f ∈ C_c^∞ [DM78].
items.note: Routed to AF.1, which builds smooth Fréchet globalizations.
